message.content:
I don’t have a live API to pull the official Canadian holiday calendar directly, but I can give you a quick rundown of the long‑weekend dates that were observed in Canada during 2023. These are based on the federal holidays that fall on or adjacent to weekends, plus the provincial holidays that create extended weekends in certain regions.

| Date | Holiday | Long‑Weekend (Typical) | Notes |
|------|---------|------------------------|-------|
| **Jan 1 2023** | New Year’s Day | **Jan 1–3** (Sunday–Tuesday) | New Year’s Day fell on a Sunday, so the public holiday was observed on Monday, Jan 2. |
| **Feb 20 2023** | Family Day (Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario) | **Feb 18–20** (Saturday–Monday) | Family Day is a provincial holiday; it created a long weekend in those provinces. |
| **Apr 7 2023** | Good Friday | **Apr 7–9** (Friday–Sunday) | Good Friday is a federal holiday; the weekend is naturally extended. |
| **May 22 2023** | Victoria Day | **May 20–22** (Saturday–Monday) | Victoria Day is a federal holiday celebrated on the Monday preceding May 25. |
| **Jul 1 2023** | Canada Day | **Jul 1–3** (Saturday–Monday) | Canada Day fell on a Saturday; the public holiday was observed on Monday, Jul 2. |
| **Sep 4 2023** | Labour Day | **Sep 2–4** (Saturday–Monday) | Labour Day is a federal holiday on the first Monday in September. |
| **Oct 9 2023** | Thanksgiving | **Oct 7–9** (Saturday–Monday) | Thanksgiving is a federal holiday on the second Monday in October. |
| **Nov 11 2023** | Remembrance Day | **Nov 11–13** (Saturday–Monday) | Remembrance Day is a federal holiday on November 11; the public holiday was observed on Monday, Nov 13. |
| **Dec 25 2023** | Christmas Day | **Dec 25–27** (Monday–Wednesday) | Christmas Day is a federal holiday on December 25. |
| **Dec 26 2023** | Boxing Day | **Dec 26–28** (Tuesday–Thursday) | Boxing Day is a federal holiday on December 26. |

### How to Use This List

1. **Filter by Province** – If you’re planning trips in a specific province, keep only the holidays that apply there (e.g., Family Day only applies to Alberta, BC, Saskatchewan, and Ontario).
2. **Add Extra Days** – Some people take an extra day off (e.g., the Monday after a holiday) to create a 4‑day weekend. Adjust your planning accordingly.
3. **Check Local Variations** – Certain provinces have additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, or Civic Holiday in Ontario). Add those if relevant.

If you need a more detailed, official list (including provincial holidays and exact dates for each province), you can consult the Government of Canada’s public holiday calendar or the provincial government websites. Let me know if you’d like help pulling that data from a specific source!
